title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is page 8 of a manuscript in the 'Longue Marche' circle (c. 1981). It sets up the birational anabelian programme for fields K finitely generated over Q.

Setting. Let K be finitely generated over Q, and let k be the algebraic closure of Q in K (the field of constants). Fix an algebraic closure K̄ of K. Write:
- Γ = Γ_{k̄|k} = Gal(k̄/k);
- π = π_{K̄|K} = π_1(Spec(K ⊗_k k̄)) = Gal(K̄/K k̄), the geometric fundamental group of the generic point η = Spec K.

The extension and its reconstruction. The previous page notes that π is centre-free. The arithmetic group E_{K̄/K} = Gal(K̄/K) is an extension 1 → π → E → Γ → 1. Because π is centre-free, this extension is determined up to unique isomorphism by its outer action φ: Γ → Autext(π) = Out(π). Concretely, E is the pullback (fibre product) of the universal extension
(15) 1 → π → Aut(π) → Autext(π) → 1
along φ. This is classical Schreier / Eilenberg–MacLane extension theory: with Z(π) = 1, extensions inducing a given outer action exist and are unique up to unique isomorphism.

What is being fixed. Grothendieck then analyses the rigidifying data. Fixing Γ amounts to fixing an algebraic closure k̄ of k. Fixing π amounts to fixing a universal cover of Spec(K ⊗_k k̄) = η ⊗_k k̄. Together these two choices amount exactly to giving the universal cover η̄ = Spec(K̄) of η. Conversely, K̄ determines k̄ as the algebraic closure of k inside it.

The programme. He proposes to describe pairs (K, K̄), 'with a fidelity that remains to be examined', by triples (π, Γ, φ): two profinite groups and an outer action. This is the birational anabelian reconstruction problem, stated in its 'outer Galois action' form.

The next page corrects the setup: Γ must also be given as a subgroup of a fixed Gal(Q̄/Q), i.e. as an open subgroup acting on a point of Π_Q. The aim is to recover the morphism of pro-Galois topoi B_K → B_Q together with a point.
errors: The omission that Γ must be embedded in a fixed Gal(Q̄/Q) (needed to recover K over Q, and not just up to 'twists') is acknowledged by Grothendieck himself on the next page.

Centre-freeness of π: when K = k (transcendence degree 0), π is trivial and trivially centre-free. In positive dimension π is the absolute Galois group of a function field over an algebraically closed field, which is indeed centre-free. No error, but this is assumed rather than proved here.
The 'fidelity' of the description is left open. This is the birational Grothendieck conjecture, later proved by Pop, building on Neukirch–Uchida.

ideas.what: An extension of profinite groups with centre-free kernel is the pullback of 1→π→Aut(π)→Out(π)→1 along the outer action
ideas.modern_name: Schreier theory / extensions with centre-free kernel; Gal(K) as fibre product over Out(π)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Schreier; Eilenberg–MacLane (1940s); standard in anabelian geometry
ideas.where_published: Implicit in the Letter to Faltings (1983) and La Longue Marche; standard group theory

ideas.what: Fixing K̄ is equivalent to fixing k̄ together with a universal cover of η⊗_k k̄ (base point bookkeeping for the arithmetic vs. geometric fundamental group)
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental exact sequence 1→π_1^geom→π_1^arith→G_k→1 with base points

ideas.what: Encoding finitely generated fields K/Q (with an algebraic closure) by triples (π, Γ, φ: Γ→Out(π)), with faithfulness to be examined
ideas.modern_name: Birational anabelian conjecture (Grothendieck conjecture for function fields)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (conjecture, 1983 letter / Esquisse); proved by Pop (1990s), with Neukirch–Uchida and Mochizuki for related cases
ideas.where_published: Letter to G. Faltings (1983); Esquisse d'un programme (1984)

deep.surprise_reason: This is foundational bookkeeping for the birational anabelian programme: classical extension theory for centre-free kernels plus base-point conventions. The idea is well documented in Grothendieck's letter to Faltings and the Esquisse, and the conjecture was later proved by Pop. Nothing here goes beyond the known record.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'en termes de l'action extérieure correspondante' — 'action extérieure' is underlined in the original.
'dire qu'on fixe un π_{K̄|K} = π_1(K⊗_k k̄)' — the stray '{+est+}' insertion is likely just a mark over the π symbol rather than a word.
'[-compatible-]' is a struck-out word (perhaps 'compatibilité') before 'les deux ensembles'.
'Γ = Γ_{k̄|k}' in the triple line is an interlinear addition: 'où π = π_{K̄|K} et Γ = Γ_{k̄|k} sont des groupes profinis'.
